main.description: One founder's claim about how a namespace starts: who's eligible and what the starting policy is for each governed class. ESS_MESH_SPEC.md 3.7.2 always said this state is 'bootstrapped at namespace creation by whoever founds it' but never gave it a record type -- this is that record. Every founder writes their own claim at the same fixed key ('self') under their own author, so multiple co-founders can each post one without colliding: the (namespace, author, key) tuple already makes forging or overwriting someone else's claim impossible (SPEC.md 3.4). A reader resolves possibly-multiple claims into one genesis state by taking the earliest claim's createdAt as t0 and unioning eligibility only from claims within a bounded window of t0 (default one hour, itself namespace-owned like every other governance number) -- a claim posted well outside that window is a later member trying to backdate themselves into genesis and is ignored for that purpose; they need a real admitCoSigner Proposal instead, same as anyone else joining later. Starting policy is taken only from the earliest claim, not unioned or arbitrated among co-founders.

eligible.description: Hex-encoded author ids this founder is declaring eligible at genesis, themselves included.

policy.description: This founder's claimed starting policy for all three governed classes -- unlike a changePolicy Proposal's policyChange (network.essmesh.governance.proposal), every field here is required: a Founding claim has to fully specify where the namespace starts, not partially amend it.

createdAt.description: Self-reported, same trust boundary every other createdAt field in these lexicons already has -- a founder can only lie about their own founding time, which only ever hurts their own claim's chance of falling inside another co-founder's acceptance window, not anyone else's.
